Definition: literally one officiating, a priest; also (by courtesy) an acting priest (although a layman)
KeyPassages: Genesis 14:18; Exodus 2:16; Leviticus 1:5; Numbers 3:3; Deuteronomy 17:9; Joshua 3:3
BiblicalUsage: Kohen is a priest, one who officiates. Genesis 14:18 introduces Melchizedek, priest of the most high God, bringing bread and wine, Exodus 2:16 names the priest of Midian with his seven daughters, Leviticus 1:5 has Aaron's sons bringing the blood to sprinkle on the altar, Numbers 3:3 names the priests anointed to minister, Deuteronomy 17:9 sends the hard case to the priests the Levites, and Joshua 3:3 has the priests bearing the ark of the covenant before the people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the priest is the man who stands between: Melchizedek brings bread and wine, Aaron's sons bring blood, and the Levites carry the ark ahead of the people. I hold that every priest in these verses is a shadow of the one Priest who does not stand between by office but by His own blood.
RelatedBooks: Genesis; Exodus; Leviticus; Numbers; Deuteronomy; Joshua
